Compare hot days in an early period with a recent period

Source: R/compare-periods.R
compare_periods.Rd

Summarises the output of count_hot_days() for two non-overlapping periods, so a user can see whether very hot fire-season days have become more common. Only complete seasons (see the complete column) are used, because a season with many missing days would undercount hot days.

Usage

compare_periods(
  hot_days,
  early = c(1910, 1939),
  recent = c(1989, 2018),
  min_seasons = 10
)

Arguments

hot_days

A tibble returned by count_hot_days() or count_exceedances().

early

Two years giving the first and last season of the early period. Defaults to c(1910, 1939).

recent

Two years giving the first and last season of the recent period. Defaults to c(1989, 2018), the last 30 complete seasons. 30 years is the standard length used to describe a climate "average".

min_seasons

The fewest complete seasons a period needs before its average is treated as reliable. Defaults to 10.

Value

A tibble with two rows ("Early" and "Recent") and columns:

period

"Early" or "Recent".

first_season, last_season

The years requested.

seasons_used

Complete seasons inside the period.

mean_hot_days

Average counted days per complete season (NA if there are none). The name is kept for both inputs.

enough_data

TRUE when seasons_used is at least min_seasons.

Examples

melb <- count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Melbourne")
compare_periods(melb)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   period first_season last_season seasons_used mean_hot_days enough_data
#>   <chr>         <int>       <int>        <int>         <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1 Early          1910        1939           30          7.57 TRUE       
#> 2 Recent         1989        2018           30          8.83 TRUE       
# Average days of 35 degrees C or more per season, early versus recent

# Brisbane's record starts in 1949, so an early period before then
# has no seasons and is flagged with enough_data = FALSE
count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Brisbane") |>
  compare_periods(early = c(1910, 1939))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   period first_season last_season seasons_used mean_hot_days enough_data
#>   <chr>         <int>       <int>        <int>         <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1 Early          1910        1939            0        NA     FALSE      
#> 2 Recent         1989        2018           30         0.833 TRUE
